Step 1 Reaction of trans-cinnamaldehyde with CH₃MgBr  
trans-Cinnamaldehyde = Ph-CH=CH-CHO (9 C atoms).  
A Grignard reagent adds by 1,2-addition to the aldehyde carbonyl.  
Ph-CH=CH-CHO  +  CH₃MgBr  →  Ph-CH=CH-CH(OH)CH₃ (product 1)  
Carbon atoms: 9 + 1 (from CH₃) = 10 C.

Step 2 Oxidation of 1 with PCC  
PCC converts the secondary alcohol to the corresponding ketone without changing the carbon skeleton.  
Ph-CH=CH-COCH₃ (product 2)  
Carbon atoms remain 10.

Step 3 Reaction of 2 with (CH₃)₂S(O)=CH₂ (dimethyl(oxo)-λ⁶-sulfaneylidene)methane)  
This sulfur ylide (Corey–Chaykovsky reagent) reacts with carbonyl compounds to give epoxides, adding its methylene (CH₂) to the carbonyl carbon.  
Ph-CH=CH-C(–CH₃)–CH₂  
       \ /  
       O   (product 3, an allylic epoxide)

The ylide contributes one new carbon (the methylene of the epoxide).  
Total carbons in product 3: 10 + 1 = 11.

Therefore the number of carbon atoms in product 3 is 11.

Answer: A
